report:
### Conclusion

High-quality scientific evidence demonstrates that **hydroxychloroquine does not reduce the likelihood of dying from COVID-19**.

While early laboratory cell-culture studies suggested potential antiviral properties, large-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews found no clinical efficacy:

* **RECOVERY Trial:** A large RCT published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* assigned 1,561 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to hydroxychloroquine and 3,155 to standard care. Hydroxychloroquine did not lower 28-day mortality and was associated with longer hospital stays and an increased risk of progressing to invasive mechanical ventilation or death.
* **WHO Solidarity Trial:** An international trial across 30 countries found that hydroxychloroquine had little to no effect on overall mortality, initiation of mechanical ventilation, or duration of hospital stay among hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
* **Cochrane Review:** A systematic review synthesizing data across multiple clinical trials confirmed that hydroxychloroquine produces no clinical benefit in reducing deaths from COVID-19 while increasing the risk of adverse health events.

Because rigorous trials consistently show no mortality benefit, major health bodies, including the World Health Organization, advise against using hydroxychloroquine for COVID-19.

* [WHO - Solidarity Trial and Hydroxychloroquine Q&A](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-hydroxychloroquine)
